headline: Volume Momentum Intact; Pricing Yet to Catch Up with Costs

highlights: Key Points  Revenue ahead on volumes; RM inflation holds back margins: Ashok Leyland reported 2QFY27 standalone revenue of Rs133.6bn, up 39.4% YoY (+38.7% QoQ) and 3.4%/4.7% ahead of NBIE/consensus estimates.
EBITDA rose 16.2% YoY to Rs13.5bn, 1.9%/1.0% ahead of NBIE/consensus.
EBITDA margin declined by 202bps YoY to 10.1% (flat QoQ), 15bps/37bps below NBIE/consensus, as gross margin contracted by 373bps YoY to 25.1% on RM inflation.

PAT grew 7.1% YoY (+42.7% QoQ) to Rs8.7bn, 2.5%/3.8% below NBIE/consensus.  Outlook: Management remains constructive on the CV cycle, supported by GST 2.0-led replacement demand, an ageing vehicle fleet, improving financing availability, and infrastructure activity.
valuation: The company has undertaken a price increase in Q3 (targeting 100–150bps), with another hike likely in Q4.
FY27 capex guidance stands at Rs10–12bn, of which Rs3.9bn was incurred in H1.  Valuation: We maintain our BUY rating on Ashok Leyland with a revised TP of Rs198 (previous: Rs193).

We value the core business at 13.75x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA and HLFL at Rs14/share, arriving at a target price of Rs198. driven by its improving business mix with 45–50% of revenues contributed by higher-margin, relatively less cyclical non-CV businesses.
